title: Erdős Problem 835 when k + 1 is composite: the chromatic number of J(2k, k) exceeds k + 1
abstract: Erdős Problem 835 asks whether, for some k > 2, the k-element subsets of a 2k-element set can be coloured with k + 1 colours so that every (k + 1)-element set sees all k + 1 colours among its k-element subsets; equivalently, whether the Johnson graph J(2k, k) has chromatic number k + 1 for some k > 2. Jie Ma and Quanyu Tang showed that this fails whenever k + 1 is not prime. This Lean 4 formalization proves, with Mathlib only: the equivalence between the colouring property and χ(J(2k, k)) = k + 1 for k > 0; χ(J(2k, k)) > k + 1 for every k > 2 with k + 1 composite; the consequence for every odd k > 2; and χ(J(18, 9)) > 10. The proof is a double count of the k-subsets of one colour inside a (k + j)-set, which forces k + 1 to divide (k + j).choose j for 1 ≤ j ≤ k; a prime p < k + 1 dividing k + 1 violates this at j = p. The case where k + 1 is prime, and so the problem itself, remains open; no new mathematics is claimed.
